title: Throughput lane allocator and hardware estimate (private VPC)
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight calculator + allocation strategy for Private/VPC deployments focused on multi-region throughput lanes. Intended as a working planning sheet to translate customer SLA targets (p95 latency / RPS) into a recommended hardware purchase BOM and minimal headroom assumptions. This is not the final procurement doc — use with finance and procurement for quotes.

Executive summary (one-line):
Map customer traffic lanes to GPU node pools by latency tier and throughput density; choose node types and counts to meet steady-state throughput with 25–35% headroom and a conservative failover buffer for regional outage scenarios.

Assumptions (configurable inputs):
- Expected peak QPS (queries per second) per region: 250 QPS (example baseline)
- Average request size: 120 tokens generated per request
- Model family target: Llama-2-13B-ggml variant (quantized) with avg per-token GPU throughput of ~600 tokens/sec per A100-80GB equiv lane when using batching (empirical numbers; adjust per model)
- Desired p95 generation latency (client-facing): <= 400ms for interactive lane; <= 2s for batch lane
- Acceptable GPU avg utilization: 60% (steady), burst up to 85% for short windows
- Headroom: 30% reserved for sudden spikes and redundancy
- Node configuration options considered: 4xA100-80GB in multi-GPU box, 8xH100-80GB, 8xRTX6000 (for lower-cost), and 1xA10G for low-cost inference lanes

Inputs (cells to edit):
- REGION_LIST: [us-east1, eu-west1]
- PEAK_QPS_BY_REGION: {us-east1: 250, eu-west1: 70}
- AVG_TOKENS_PER_REQUEST: 120
- TARGET_MODEL_TOKENS_PER_SEC_PER_GPU: 600
- LATENCY_TIER: interactive | async | bulk (map to batching policy)
- TARGET_P95_LATENCY_MS: interactive=400, async=1500, bulk=5000
- GPU_UTIL_TARGET: 0.60
- HEADROOM_RATIO: 0.30

Core calculations (text formulas):
1) Required token/sec per region = PEAK_QPS * AVG_TOKENS_PER_REQUEST
   Example (us-east1): 250 * 120 = 30,000 tokens/sec
2) Effective usable tokens/sec per GPU = TARGET_MODEL_TOKENS_PER_SEC_PER_GPU * GPU_UTIL_TARGET
   Example: 600 * 0.60 = 360 tokens/sec per GPU usable for steady traffic
3) Raw GPUs needed = ceil(Required token/sec / usable tokens/sec per GPU)
   us-east1: ceil(30000 / 360) = ceil(83.33) = 84 GPUs
4) Apply headroom: Provisioned GPUs = ceil(Raw GPUs needed * (1 + HEADROOM_RATIO))
   us-east1: 84 * 1.30 = 109.2 => 110 GPUs
5) Map to node SKUs by GPU-per-node (e.g., 8x H100 per node) => nodes = ceil(provisioned_gpus / gpus_per_node)
   If using 8xH100: nodes = ceil(110 / 8) = 14 nodes
6) Add resilience buffer for regional failover (optional): additional nodes = +2 nodes or +10% of nodes (whichever larger)

Example scenario table (interactive lane, us-east1 baseline):
- Peak QPS: 250
- Avg tokens: 120
- Required tokens/sec: 30,000
- Usable tokens/sec per GPU: 360
- Raw GPUs: 84
- Headroom (30%): +26 => provisioned GPUs = 110
- Node selection: 8xH100 (recommended for highest density) => nodes = 14 + 2 resilience = 16 nodes total
- Approx per-node cost (list price est): $120k per 8xH100 node -> hardware subtotal = 16 * $120k = $1.92M (placeholder quotes needed)

Alternative for cost-sensitive customers (mixed lane):
- Put interactive latency-critical lane on H100 (8x), move async/batch lanes to 4x A10G or 4xA100-80GB nodes to reduce cost.
- Example split: interactive (50% QPS) -> 8 H100 nodes; batch (50% QPS) -> 12 A10G nodes estimated (run separate calculations).

Packing heuristics and bin-packing notes:
- Prefer homogeneous racks per region to simplify scheduling and NVLink topologies.
- Use fractional-shared GPUs only if runtime supports MPS-like multiplexing and SLAs accept higher tail latency. We recommend whole-GPU allocation for interactive lanes.
- When mixing GPU types, enforce model-compatibility labels and set routing weight-based fallbacks in the control plane.

Network, storage, and infra add-ons (rough estimates):
- 10Gbps per node baseline for inter-node KV/replication; 25–40Gbps if streaming many small contexts
- NVMe cache per node: 1–2TB local NVMe for KV cache snapshotting and OS images
- Control-plane VM pool: 3–5 m5.4xlarge-equivalent instances per region for management, autoscaler, and rollout controllers
- Infra software license & support (Redwood private fee) — to be calculated separately

Minimal BOM template (example lines) — replace unit price with vendor quote:
- 8xH100 node (2U) | GPUs: 8 H100 80GB | vCPU: 128 | RAM: 1.5TB | NVMe: 8TB | unit_price: $120,000 | qty: 16 | line_total: $1,920,000
- 4xA100-80GB node | GPUs: 4 A100 80GB | vCPU: 64 | RAM: 768GB | NVMe: 4TB | unit_price: $48,000 | qty: 0 | line_total: $0
- A10G small inference node | GPUs: 1 A10G | vCPU: 24 | RAM: 192GB | NVMe: 1TB | unit_price: $9,000 | qty: 12 | line_total: $108,000
- Network switch 100Gbps per rack | unit_price: $25,000 | qty: 4 | line_total: $100,000
- Rack and power (PDU/cabling) | unit_price: $4,500 | qty: 6 | line_total: $27,000
- Professional services (installation + rack & stack) | flat_fee: $60,000 | qty: 1 | line_total: $60,000
- Total rough hardware estimate (example): $2,215,000

Utilization and cost-sensitivity knobs: 
- Lower avg token throughput per GPU (e.g., different model) drives GPU counts up linearly. Replace TARGET_MODEL_TOKENS_PER_SEC_PER_GPU with measured numbers from model onboarding stage.
- Increasing acceptable steady-state utilization to 70% reduces GPU needs but increases risk of tail latency and time-to-failure.
- Use caching (prefix/KV) aggressively to reduce tokens per request for stable prompts; measure cache hit % and fold into avg tokens calculation.

Region distribution and multi-region failover plan: 
- Primary region handles 80% of traffic in design scenario with a smaller DR region sized for 25–30% of normal load. For hard SLA customers, size DR at 50% and use cross-region replicas.
- Ensure cross-region egress budget is accounted for in network cost model.

Operational considerations (actionable checklist):
- [ ] Run model benchmark harness on target GPU SKUs to get accurate per-token throughput numbers (owner: Lina)
- [ ] Get vendor quotes for H100 vs A100 node SKUs (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Validate batch sizing and p95 latency in staging with traffic replay (owner: Tom)
- [ ] Update billing/finance worksheet with procurement discounts and tax (owner: Priya)

Open questions / risks: 
- How accurate are estimated tokens/sec numbers for LLM variants customers will choose? (Mitigation: run representative benchmarks)
- Procurement lead times for H100 inventory (3–16 weeks) — may influence staging and interim fallbacks
- Rack density / power availability in target colo — confirm with customer site ops before final BOM

Next steps (short-term roadmap):
1) Benchmark three model families (13B, 34B, 70B) on candidate SKUs and update TARGET_MODEL_TOKENS_PER_SEC_PER_GPU.
2) Convert this sheet into a small interactive workbook (Google Sheet) with editable inputs and dynamic outputs for sales/SE use.
3) Draft procurement-ready BOM and present to Finance + Procurement for PO estimates.

Notes and references:
- See confluence:PD-VPC-CAPACITY-2026 for historical sizers and previous procurement notes.
- See INFRA-842 and INFRA-900 for related autoscaler + routing tickets.
- Slack thread: #private-deployments (link above) for conversations about mixed-sku strategies.

Ownership & contact: Asha Menon (eng-private-deployments) — use this doc as the canonical baseline for planning; update with measured bench numbers as they arrive.

Change log (brief):
- 2025-11-03: initial draft with baseline example
- 2025-12-15: added node-level BOM template and resilience buffer recommendation
- 2026-01-12: tuned headroom to 30% and added action checklist
